```{r}
# 1. Read your data
bgc <- read_csv("bgc_class_dataset_clustering_with_taxonomy.csv")  
antismash <- read.csv("antismash_names.csv")

bgc_with_node <- bgc %>%
  mutate(
    node_clean = str_remove(orig_filename, "\\.region.*$")
  )
merged <- bgc_with_node %>%
  left_join(antismash, by = c("node_clean" = "node"))

metadata <- read_csv("Metadata_combined.csv")
metadata_long <- metadata %>%
  select(Sample_Name, Other_Name, everything()) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Sample_Name, Other_Name),
    names_to = "name_type",
    values_to = "file"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(file), file != "") %>%
  distinct(file, .keep_all = TRUE)

df_1 <- merged %>%
  left_join(metadata_long, by = "file")

nadf <- df_1 %>% filter(is.na(`cb-broad-desc`))

df <- df_1 %>% 
  filter(!is.na(`cb-broad-desc`))

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    subclass_name = case_when(
      subclass_name == "generic" & class_name == "NRP"     ~ "generic_NRP",
      subclass_name == "generic" & class_name == "Terpene" ~ "generic_Terpene",
      TRUE ~ subclass_name
    )
  )
```
```{r}

############################################################
# CASE  — BUILD ALL SAMPLE × GENUS MATRICES
############################################################

df_tax <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(file), file != "", !is.na(Genus), Genus != "")

# ---------- 1) sample × subclass_name ----------
comm_genus_df <- df_tax %>%
  count(file, Genus, name = "abundance") %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = Genus,
    values_from = abundance,
    values_fill = 0
  )
```

```{r}

############################################################
# CASE 1 — BUILD ALL SAMPLE × FEATURE MATRICES
############################################################

df_div <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(file), file != "")

# ---------- 1) sample × subclass_name ----------
comm_subclass_df <- df_div %>%
  count(file, subclass_name, name = "abundance") %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = subclass_name,
    values_from = abundance,
    values_fill = 0
  )

comm_subclass <- as.matrix(comm_subclass_df[, -1])
rownames(comm_subclass) <- comm_subclass_df$file


# ---------- 2) sample × class_name ----------
comm_class_df <- df_div %>%
  count(file, class_name, name = "abundance") %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = class_name,
    values_from = abundance,
    values_fill = 0
  )

comm_class <- as.matrix(comm_class_df[, -1])
rownames(comm_class) <- comm_class_df$file


# ---------- 3) sample × gcf_id ----------
comm_gcf_df <- df_div %>%
  count(file, gcf_id, name = "abundance") %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = gcf_id,
    values_from = abundance,
    values_fill = 0
  )

comm_gcf <- as.matrix(comm_gcf_df[, -1])
rownames(comm_gcf) <- comm_gcf_df$file
```

```{r}
############################################################
# PREP META (samplewise info)
############################################################

sample_meta <- df_div %>%
  distinct(
    file,
    Dataset,
    `cb-broad-desc`,
    `cb-narrow-desc`
  ) %>%
  rename(
    sample       = file,
    location     = Dataset,
    broad_env    = `cb-broad-desc`,
    narrow_env   = `cb-narrow-desc`
  )
```

```{r}
############################################################
# ALIGN community matrices to sample_meta ordering
############################################################

# Ensure sample order matches metadata
common_samples <- Reduce(
  intersect,
  list(
    rownames(comm_subclass),
    rownames(comm_class),
    rownames(comm_gcf),
    sample_meta$sample
  )
)

# Filter metadata first
sample_meta <- sample_meta %>%
  filter(sample %in% common_samples) %>%
  arrange(sample)

# Reorder each matrix
comm_subclass <- comm_subclass[sample_meta$sample, , drop = FALSE]
comm_class    <- comm_class[sample_meta$sample, , drop = FALSE]
comm_gcf      <- comm_gcf[sample_meta$sample, , drop = FALSE]

```

```{r}
class_summary <- df %>%
  group_by(Dataset, class_name) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop")

# 2️⃣ Plot relative % (stacked to 100)
ggplot(class_summary,
       aes(x = Dataset, y = count, fill = class_name)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") +  # <-- fill makes it % of total
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  labs(title = "Relative Distribution of BGC chemical classes by location",
       x = "Location (Dataset)",
       y = "Percent",
       fill = "Chemical class") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```



```{r}
## 1. Subclass counts per Dataset -----------------------------

subclass_summary <- df %>%
  group_by(Dataset, subclass_name) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop")

## 2. Presence/absence (0/1) matrix ---------------------------

subclass_pa <- subclass_summary %>%
  mutate(present = as.integer(count > 0)) %>%   # 0/1
  select(Dataset, subclass_name, present)

pa_df <- subclass_pa %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    id_cols     = Dataset,
    names_from  = subclass_name,
    values_from = present,
    values_fill = 0
  )

mat_pa <- as.matrix(pa_df[, -1, drop = FALSE])
rownames(mat_pa) <- pa_df$Dataset

## 3. Map subclass_name -> class_name -------------------------

subclass_class_map <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(subclass_name), !is.na(class_name)) %>%
  group_by(subclass_name) %>%
  summarise(
    class_name = paste(sort(unique(class_name)), collapse = "; "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

## 4. Build column info in the SAME order as matrix columns ---

col_info <- tibble(subclass_name = colnames(mat_pa)) %>%
  left_join(subclass_class_map, by = "subclass_name")

## 5. Define desired class order & create factor --------------

class_order <- c("NRP",
                 "Polyketide",
                 "RiPP",
                 "Saccharide",
                 "Other",
                 "Unknown")

col_info$class_name_fact <- factor(col_info$class_name,
                                   levels = class_order)

## 6. Decide final column order (by class, then subclass) -----

ord <- order(col_info$class_name_fact, col_info$subclass_name, na.last = TRUE)

col_order <- col_info$subclass_name[ord]
mat_pa    <- mat_pa[, col_order, drop = FALSE]

## 7. Build pheatmap-style annotation_col data.frame ----------

annotation_col <- data.frame(
  class_name = col_info$class_name[ord],
  row.names  = col_order,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

## 8. Plot pheatmap -------------------------------------------

pheatmap(
  mat_pa,
  cluster_rows      = TRUE,
  cluster_cols      = FALSE,          # keep our manual column order
  scale             = "none",
  color             = c("white", "blue"),
  breaks            = c(-0.5, 0.5, 1.5),
  legend_breaks     = c(0, 1),
  legend_labels     = c("Absent", "Present"),
  annotation_col    = annotation_col,
  annotation_legend = TRUE,
  border_color      = NA,
  fontsize_row      = 6,
  fontsize_col      = 6,              # smaller column labels
  main              = "Presence/Absence of BGC Subclasses"
)

```

```{r}
# 2. Total number of samples per location
total_counts <- sidephore_df %>%
  group_by(location) %>%
  summarise(total_samples = n(), .groups = "drop")

phos_df <- comm_subclass_df %>%
  select(file, phosphonate, `phosphonate-like`) %>%
  mutate(
    has_phosphonate = phosphonate > 0,
    has_phosphonate_like = `phosphonate-like` > 0,
    any_phos = has_phosphonate | has_phosphonate_like
  )
phos_df$location = sample_meta$location
phos_df$broad_env = sample_meta$broad_env
phos_samples <- phos_df %>% filter(any_phos == TRUE)

phos_counts <- phos_df %>%
  filter(any_phos == TRUE) %>%
  group_by(location) %>%
  summarise(n_phos_samples = n())


phos_samples <- phos_samples %>%
  mutate(phos_total = phosphonate + `phosphonate-like`)
phos_samples <- phos_samples %>%
  left_join(phos_counts, by = "location") %>%
  left_join(total_counts,      by = "location") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(location, " (", n_phos_samples,  "/", total_samples, ")"))


ggplot(phos_samples, aes(x = label, y = phos_total, fill = broad_env)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Phosphonate-type BGC Counts per Sample",
    x = "Environment (phosphonate-positive sample count)",
    y = "Total phosphonate-like BGCs"
  )

```

```{r}
subset_phos <- df %>% 
  filter(subclass_name %in% c("phosphonate", "phosphonate-like")) %>%
  select(file, Dataset, gcf_id)


edge_df <- subset_phos %>%
  select(file, gcf_id) %>%
  inner_join(., ., by = "gcf_id") %>%   # all pairs sharing the same gcf_id
  filter(file.x < file.y) %>%           # avoid duplicates & self-pairs
  transmute(from = file.x, to = file.y) %>%
  distinct()

# Node table: one row per sample
node_df <- subset_phos %>%
  select(file, Dataset) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  rename(name = file)

# 1. Make graph using only edges
g <- graph_from_data_frame(edge_df, directed = FALSE)

# 2. Add Dataset as a vertex attribute
V(g)$Dataset <- node_df$Dataset[match(V(g)$name, node_df$name)]

# Plot
ggraph(g, layout = "fr") +
  geom_edge_link(alpha = 0.3, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_node_point(aes(color = Dataset), size = 4) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title    = "Phosphonate GCF Network",
    subtitle = "Nodes = samples, edges = shared GCF IDs",
    color    = "Dataset"
  )

```

```{r}
# 1. Subset and flag siderophore-positive samples
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
#Dim Reduction plot for total Samples
set.seed(0)
# Use the aligned community matrix
df.data <- as.data.frame(comm_subclass)

# Metadata
Sample_Type  <- sample_meta$location
Sample_Names <- sample_meta$sample

# UMAP (uwot::umap returns a matrix)
df.umap <- umap(df.data, n_components = 2)

# Convert result to data.frame
df_out <- as.data.frame(df.umap)
colnames(df_out) <- c("UMAP1", "UMAP2")
df_out$Sample_Type  <- Sample_Type
df_out$Sample_Names <- Sample_Names

# Plot
ggplot(df_out, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = Sample_Type)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  # if you have a custom palette:
  # scale_color_manual(values = color_multi) +
  stat_conf_ellipse(level = 0.9999) +
  ggtitle("BGC subclass diversity vs location")

```

```{r}
#Calculating alpha diversity class
sample_meta$alpha_simpson_class <-  diversity(comm_class_df[, -1], index = "simpson")
sample_meta$alpha_shannon_class <-  diversity(comm_class_df[, -1], index = "shannon")
sample_meta$alpha_invsimpson_class <- diversity(comm_class_df[, -1], index = "invsimpson")
sample_meta$richness_class <- specnumber(comm_class_df[, -1])

#Calculating alpha diversity subclass
sample_meta$alpha_simpson_subclass <-  diversity(comm_subclass_df[, -1], index = "simpson")
sample_meta$alpha_shannon_subclass <-  diversity(comm_subclass_df[, -1], index = "shannon")
sample_meta$alpha_invsimpson_subclass <- diversity(comm_subclass_df[, -1], index = "invsimpson")
sample_meta$richness_subclass <- specnumber(comm_subclass_df[, -1])

#Calculating alpha diversity gcf
sample_meta$alpha_simpson_gcf <-  diversity(comm_gcf_df[, -1], index = "simpson")
sample_meta$alpha_shannon_gcf <-  diversity(comm_gcf_df[, -1], index = "shannon")
sample_meta$alpha_invsimpson_gcf <- diversity(comm_gcf_df[, -1], index = "invsimpson")
sample_meta$richness_gcf <- specnumber(comm_gcf_df[, -1])

```

```{r}
run_pairwise_mw <- function(data, value_col, group_col, p_cutoff = 0.05) {
  # Lazily evaluate column names
  value <- data[[value_col]]
  group <- data[[group_col]]
  
  # Step 1: Run pairwise Wilcoxon tests
  mw_res <- pairwise.wilcox.test(
    x = value,
    g = group,
    p.adjust.method = "BH"
  )
  
  # Step 2: Convert matrix to tidy tibble
  tidy_res <- as.data.frame(as.table(mw_res$p.value)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Freq)) %>%
    rename(
      group1  = Var1,
      group2  = Var2,
      p_value = Freq
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      p_adj    = p_value,
      label    = paste0("p=", signif(p_adj, 3)),
      sig_star = case_when(
        p_adj < 0.001 ~ "***",
        p_adj < 0.01  ~ "**",
        p_adj < 0.05  ~ "*",
        TRUE          ~ "ns"
      )
    ) %>%
    filter(p_adj < p_cutoff)  # keep only significant pairs
  
  return(tidy_res)
}
```

```{r}
mds_data <- as.data.frame(mds_class$points) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(sample = comm_class_df$file) %>%   # add sample IDs
  dplyr::left_join(
    sample_meta %>% dplyr::select(sample, location, broad_env),
    by = "sample"
  )

ggplot(mds_data, aes(x = MDS1, y = MDS2, color = location)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_conf_ellipse(level = 0.95) +   # 95% ellipses are usually more sensible than 99.99%
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Bray–Curtis Beta Diversity (BGC class)",
    x = "NMDS1",
    y = "NMDS2",
    color = "Location"
```

```{r}
perm <- adonis2(beta_dist_class ~ broad_env, data = sample_meta, permutations = 999)
bd <- betadisper(beta_dist_class, sample_meta$broad_env)
anova(bd)                 # test significance
TukeyHSD(bd)              # which groups differ
```


```{r}
# Panel A: Boxplot with key comparisons
disp_df <- data.frame(
  environment = sample_meta$broad_env,
  dispersion = bd$distances
)

ggplot(disp_df, aes(x = reorder(environment, dispersion, median), 
                          y = dispersion, fill = environment)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, size = 0.8, alpha = 0.3) +
  
  # Highlight sludge (lowest dispersion)
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(disp_df$dispersion[disp_df$environment == "sludge"]),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = max(disp_df$dispersion) * 0.95,
           label = "Sludge: most homogeneous\n(lowest dispersion)",
           hjust = 0, size = 4, color = "red", fontface = "bold") +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "A. Dispersion by Environment",
    x = "Environment (ordered by median dispersion)",
    y = "Distance to Centroid"
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo")

```

```{r}
# Panel B: Significant pairwise comparisons
tukey_df <- as.data.frame(TukeyHSD(bd)$group)
tukey_df$comparison <- rownames(tukey_df)

sig_comparisons <- tukey_df %>%
  filter(`p adj` < 0.05) %>%
  arrange(`p adj`) %>%
  head(10) %>%  # Top 10 most significant
  mutate(
    comparison = factor(comparison, levels = comparison),
    sig_level = case_when(
      `p adj` < 0.001 ~ "p < 0.001",
      `p adj` < 0.01  ~ "p < 0.01",
      TRUE            ~ "p < 0.05"
    )
  )

ggplot(sig_comparisons, aes(x = diff, y = reorder(comparison, diff), 
                                  color = sig_level)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lwr, xmax = upr), height = 0.3, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "B. Top 10 Significant Pairwise Differences",
    x = "Difference in Dispersion (95% CI)",
    y = "Comparison",
    color = "Significance"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("p < 0.001" = "firebrick",
                                 "p < 0.01" = "orange",
                                 "p < 0.05" = "steelblue"))
```


```{r}
perm <- adonis2(beta_dist_class ~ location, data = sample_meta, permutations = 999)
bd <- betadisper(beta_dist_class, sample_meta$location)
anova(bd)                 # test significance
TukeyHSD(bd)              # which groups differ
```


```{r}
# Panel B: Significant pairwise comparisons
tukey_df <- as.data.frame(TukeyHSD(bd)$group)
tukey_df$comparison <- rownames(tukey_df)

sig_comparisons <- tukey_df %>%
  filter(`p adj` < 0.05) %>%
  arrange(`p adj`) %>%
  head(10) %>%  # Top 10 most significant
  mutate(
    comparison = factor(comparison, levels = comparison),
    sig_level = case_when(
      `p adj` < 0.001 ~ "p < 0.001",
      `p adj` < 0.01  ~ "p < 0.01",
      TRUE            ~ "p < 0.05"
    )
  )

ggplot(sig_comparisons, aes(x = diff, y = reorder(comparison, diff), 
                                  color = sig_level)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lwr, xmax = upr), height = 0.3, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "B. Top 10 Significant Pairwise Differences",
    x = "Difference in Dispersion (95% CI)",
    y = "Comparison",
    color = "Significance"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("p < 0.001" = "firebrick",
                                 "p < 0.01" = "orange",
                                 "p < 0.05" = "steelblue"))
```
